explanation_en: This common collocation is used to describe a political figure or party taking office or assuming control of a government. While 'llegar' means 'to arrive' and 'poder' means 'power', together they form a standard set phrase. It is more natural in political contexts than 'tomar el poder', which often implies a coup or forceful takeover.

examples.en_text: The new president promised to improve the economy when he came to power.
examples.target_text: El nuevo presidente prometió mejorar la economía cuando llegó al poder.

examples.en_text: Since that party came to power, things have changed a lot in the country.
examples.target_text: Desde que ese partido llegó al poder, las cosas han cambiado mucho en el país.

examples.en_text: Many wonder what will happen if the opposition comes to power in the next elections.
examples.target_text: Muchos se preguntan qué pasará si la oposición llega al poder en las próximas elecciones.

examples.en_text: The dictator came to power after a coup d'état in the seventies.
examples.target_text: El dictador llegó al poder tras un golpe de Estado en los años setenta.

examples.en_text: How did that candidate manage to come to power without the support of the media?
examples.target_text: ¿Cómo logró ese candidato llegar al poder sin el apoyo de los medios?

examples.en_text: I don't think it will be easy for them to come to power without a strong campaign.
examples.target_text: No creo que sea fácil para ellos llegar al poder sin una campaña fuerte.

explanation_en: This is a high-level consecutive conjunction used to express the manner in which an action is performed to achieve a specific result. It is equivalent to 'de manera que' or 'de forma que' and is followed by the subjunctive mood when expressing purpose or intended result, as seen here with 'sean'. It is highly useful in formal speech, essays, and presentations to connect ideas smoothly.

examples.en_text: She organized her desk in such a way that now she can find everything quickly.
examples.target_text: Ordenó su escritorio de tal modo que ahora puede encontrar todo rápidamente.

examples.en_text: You have to cut the vegetables in such a way that they cook at the same time.
examples.target_text: Tienes que cortar las verduras de tal modo que se cocinen al mismo tiempo.

examples.en_text: He always speaks in such a way that everyone feels comfortable around him.
examples.target_text: Siempre habla de tal modo que todos se sienten cómodos a su alrededor.

examples.en_text: Explain the plan in such a way that no doubts remain about the budget.
examples.target_text: Explica el plan de tal modo que no queden dudas sobre el presupuesto.

examples.en_text: The hotel was located in such a way that we could see the sea from the window.
examples.target_text: El hotel estaba ubicado de tal modo que podíamos ver el mar desde la ventana.

examples.en_text: We must review the topic in such a way that we can pass the exam without problems.
examples.target_text: Debemos repasar el tema de tal modo que podamos aprobar el examen sin problemas.

explanation_en: This adverbial locution means 'completely', 'directly', or 'fully'. It is often used with verbs like 'afectar' (to affect), 'dar' (to hit), or 'chocar' (to crash) to emphasize the direct and total impact of an action. In everyday speech and news, it adds a strong nuance of being hit 'squarely' or 'head-on' by a situation.

examples.en_text: The sun is shining directly on my face and I can't see anything.
examples.target_text: El sol me da de pleno en la cara y no puedo ver nada.

examples.en_text: The economic crisis fully affected the small businesses in the neighborhood.
examples.target_text: La crisis económica afectó de pleno a los pequeños negocios del barrio.

examples.en_text: We have already fully entered winter and it is very cold.
examples.target_text: Ya hemos entrado de pleno en el invierno y hace muchísimo frío.

examples.en_text: The ball hit him squarely in the head during the soccer match.
examples.target_text: El balón le dio de pleno en la cabeza durante el partido de fútbol.

examples.en_text: I fully agree with your opinion on this matter, you are completely right.
examples.target_text: Coincido de pleno con tu opinión sobre este tema, tienes toda la razón.

examples.en_text: Tomorrow I have to dive fully into the company's new project.
examples.target_text: Mañana me tengo que meter de pleno en el nuevo proyecto de la empresa.

explanation_en: This common idiomatic expression is used to emphasize that an action should start immediately or is already valid from the present moment. It is synonymous with 'desde ahora mismo' or 'inmediatamente'. While simple, it is highly idiomatic and adds a native flow to both spoken and written Spanish, especially when discussing future plans or immediate requirements.

examples.en_text: I thank you in advance for your help with the move next weekend.
examples.target_text: Te agradezco desde ya tu ayuda con la mudanza del próximo fin de semana.

examples.en_text: I'm telling you right now that I am not going to tolerate that kind of behavior in my house.
examples.target_text: Desde ya te digo que no voy a aceptar ese tipo de comportamiento en mi casa.

examples.en_text: We have to start preparing the project right now if we want to deliver it on time.
examples.target_text: Tenemos que empezar a preparar el proyecto desde ya si queremos entregarlo a tiempo.

examples.en_text: You can make your reservation right now to secure your spot at the event.
examples.target_text: Puedes hacer tu reserva desde ya para asegurar tu lugar en el evento.

examples.en_text: From this moment on, we must make it clear who is going to be in charge of each task.
examples.target_text: Desde ya debemos dejar claro quién se va a encargar de cada tarea.

examples.en_text: I've decided that I'm going to eat healthier starting right now, I'm not going to wait until Monday.
examples.target_text: He decidido que voy a comer más sano desde ya, no voy a esperar al lunes.

explanation_en: This idiomatic verbal phrase means that a process, project, or event has started and is currently active or in progress. It comes from the literal movement of a machine or vehicle ('poner en marcha' means to start an engine). It is widely used in business, news, and daily life to describe ongoing plans or operations.

examples.en_text: The new project is already underway and we hope to see results soon.
examples.target_text: El nuevo proyecto ya está en marcha y esperamos ver resultados pronto.

examples.en_text: The film festival is already underway, so you can buy your tickets.
examples.target_text: El festival de cine ya está en marcha, así que puedes comprar tus entradas.

examples.en_text: All the preparations for the wedding are underway.
examples.target_text: Todos los preparativos para la boda están en marcha.

examples.en_text: The police investigation is underway to find out what happened.
examples.target_text: La investigación de la policía está en marcha para descubrir qué pasó.

examples.en_text: The office renovations are already underway and will finish next month.
examples.target_text: Las reformas en la oficina ya están en marcha y terminarán el próximo mes.

examples.en_text: The vaccination campaign is underway across the whole country.
examples.target_text: La campaña de vacunación está en marcha en todo el país.

explanation_en: The verb 'quedar' is used here as a verb of change or result (semi-copulative), indicating the state in which something ends up after an event. 'Inutilizado' means made useless or non-functional. This collocation is highly common in news, technical, and formal contexts to describe infrastructure, roads, or equipment that can no longer be used due to damage or conflict.

examples.en_text: After falling into the water, Juan's mobile phone was rendered completely useless.
examples.target_text: Tras caerse al agua, el teléfono móvil de Juan quedó completamente inutilizado.

examples.en_text: The bridge was disabled after the earthquake and cars cannot pass.
examples.target_text: El puente quedó inutilizado después del terremoto y los coches no pueden pasar.

examples.en_text: If you don't clean the coffee maker regularly, the machine can be rendered useless.
examples.target_text: Si no limpias la cafetera regularmente, la máquina puede quedar inutilizada.

examples.en_text: The credit cards were rendered useless because the magnetic chip was damaged.
examples.target_text: Las tarjetas de crédito quedaron inutilizadas porque se dañó el chip magnético.

examples.en_text: Due to the traffic accident, both of his arms were temporarily disabled.
examples.target_text: Debido al accidente de tráfico, sus dos brazos quedaron temporalmente inutilizados.

examples.en_text: My email account was disabled after they tried to hack it.
examples.target_text: Mi cuenta de correo electrónico quedó inutilizada después de que intentaran hackearla.

explanation_en: This formal idiomatic construction means to be the recipient, target, or subject of a particular action (usually negative, like attacks, criticism, or praise). It is a passive-like construction that sounds much more natural and sophisticated in written and formal spoken Spanish than using direct passive verbs. Common collocations include 'ser objeto de críticas' (to be criticized) or 'ser objeto de burlas' (to be mocked).

examples.en_text: The mayor was the subject of harsh criticism after his latest decision.
examples.target_text: El alcalde fue objeto de duras críticas tras su última decisión.

examples.en_text: This natural phenomenon has been the subject of study for many years.
examples.target_text: Este fenómeno natural ha sido objeto de estudio durante muchos años.

examples.en_text: No employee should be the target of mockery in their workplace.
examples.target_text: Ningún empleado debería ser objeto de burlas en su lugar de trabajo.

examples.en_text: The actress was the subject of many rumors before confirming her wedding.
examples.target_text: La actriz fue objeto de muchos rumores antes de confirmar su boda.

examples.en_text: The suspect is the subject of a police investigation at this moment.
examples.target_text: El sospechoso es objeto de una investigación policial en este momento.

examples.en_text: The Mona Lisa painting continues to be the subject of debate among historians.
examples.target_text: El cuadro de la Mona Lisa sigue siendo objeto de debate entre los historiadores.

explanation_en: Literally meaning 'period' or 'full stop' at the end of a text, this noun phrase is idiomatically used to signal the absolute end of something, such as a discussion, a relationship, a project, or a broadcast. In media, it is a common way to close a segment. In daily life, 'poner punto final a algo' means to bring something to a definitive close.

examples.en_text: It's time to put an end to this discussion and make a decision.
examples.target_text: Es hora de poner punto final a esta discusión y tomar una decisión.

examples.en_text: With this agreement, the two countries put an end to the conflict.
examples.target_text: Con este acuerdo, los dos países pusieron punto final al conflicto.

examples.en_text: Remember to write a period at the end of the paragraph.
examples.target_text: Recuerda escribir un punto final al terminar el párrafo.

examples.en_text: I want to put an end to my time at this company and look for new challenges.
examples.target_text: Quiero poner un punto final a mi etapa en esta empresa y buscar nuevos retos.

examples.en_text: His last novel was the perfect ending to a great literary career.
examples.target_text: Su última novela fue el punto final perfecto para una gran carrera literaria.

examples.en_text: We can't keep fighting over this; we have to put an end to it today.
examples.target_text: No podemos seguir peleando por esto; hay que ponerle punto final hoy mismo.

idiom: se me viene a la mente
explanation_en: This expression is used when a thought, memory, or idea suddenly occurs to someone. It is a very common, natural alternative to 'pensar en' or 'recordar'. The verb 'venirse' is used pronominally with an indirect object pronoun (me, te, le, etc.) to indicate to whom the thought occurs.

examples.en_text: When I think about vacations, the beach of my childhood always comes to my mind.
examples.target_text: Cuando pienso en las vacaciones, siempre se me viene a la mente la playa de mi infancia.

examples.en_text: I was looking for my keys when suddenly it came to my mind that I left them in the car.
examples.target_text: Estaba buscando mis llaves cuando de repente se me vino a la mente que las dejé en el coche.

examples.en_text: If you ask me about my favorite movies, at least three science fiction ones come to my mind.
examples.target_text: Si me preguntas por mis películas favoritas, se me vienen a la mente al menos tres de ciencia ficción.

examples.en_text: The name of that actor doesn't come to my mind, but I know he is very famous.
examples.target_text: No se me viene a la mente el nombre de ese actor, pero sé que es muy famoso.

examples.en_text: Every time I hear that song, the trip we took together comes to my mind.
examples.target_text: Cada vez que escucho esa canción, se me viene a la mente el viaje que hicimos juntos.

examples.en_text: When I saw the old photo, many happy memories came to my mind.
examples.target_text: Cuando vi la foto antigua, se me vinieron a la mente muchos recuerdos felices.

explanation_en: This adverbial phrase means 'somehow' or 'by one means or another.' It is highly common in both spoken and written Spanish to express that an outcome will be achieved regardless of the specific method. Note the use of 'u' instead of 'o' before 'otra' to avoid cacophony.

examples.en_text: We have to finish this project today one way or another.
examples.target_text: Tenemos que terminar este proyecto hoy de una u otra manera.

examples.en_text: In the end, the truth always comes to light one way or another.
examples.target_text: Al final, la verdad siempre sale a la luz de una u otra manera.

examples.en_text: Don't worry, we will help you get out of this trouble one way or another.
examples.target_text: No te preocupes, te ayudaremos a salir de este problema de una u otra manera.

examples.en_text: She is determined to get that job one way or another.
examples.target_text: Ella está decidida a conseguir ese trabajo de una u otra manera.

examples.en_text: We will have to save money one way or another for the vacation.
examples.target_text: Tendremos que ahorrar dinero de una u otra manera para las vacaciones.

examples.en_text: We always stay in touch one way or another, despite the distance.
examples.target_text: Siempre nos mantenemos en contacto de una u otra manera, a pesar de la distancia.

explanation_en: This is a formal adverbial locution meaning 'previously' or 'before.' While 'antes' is more common in everyday speech, 'con anterioridad' is widely used in news, legal, and professional contexts to establish a clear timeline. It is often followed by 'a' (e.g., 'con anterioridad a la reunión') to mean 'prior to.'

examples.en_text: It is better to reserve the tickets beforehand to avoid the lines.
examples.target_text: Es mejor reservar las entradas con anterioridad para evitar las colas.

examples.en_text: The director had already read the report previously.
examples.target_text: El director ya había leído el informe con anterioridad.

examples.en_text: If you can't come to the dinner, please let me know beforehand.
examples.target_text: Si no puedes venir a la cena, por favor avísame con anterioridad.

examples.en_text: The exam topics were explained previously in class.
examples.target_text: Los temas del examen se explicaron con anterioridad en clase.

examples.en_text: As I mentioned to you previously, I won't be available on Friday.
examples.target_text: Como te mencioné con anterioridad, no estaré disponible el viernes.

examples.en_text: I had never used this application previously, but it seems very easy.
examples.target_text: Nunca había usado esta aplicación con anterioridad, pero parece muy fácil.

explanation_en: This prepositional phrase is used to indicate that an action is done to help or profit a specific group, person, or cause. It is a standard collocation in political, economic, and social discourse. It can be used interchangeably with 'para el beneficio de' but is more concise.

examples.en_text: The city council decided to change the traffic for the benefit of pedestrians.
examples.target_text: El ayuntamiento decidió cambiar el tráfico en beneficio de los peatones.

examples.en_text: We must work together for the benefit of the common project.
examples.target_text: Debemos trabajar juntos en beneficio del proyecto común.

examples.en_text: I have decided to reduce my sugar intake for the benefit of my health.
examples.target_text: He decidido reducir el consumo de azúcar en beneficio de mi salud.

examples.en_text: The teachers changed the schedule for the benefit of the students who work.
examples.target_text: Los profesores cambiaron el horario en beneficio de los estudiantes que trabajan.

examples.en_text: The company took difficult measures for the benefit of its financial stability.
examples.target_text: La empresa tomó medidas difíciles en beneficio de su estabilidad financiera.

examples.en_text: All the money raised at the event will be used for the benefit of homeless animals.
examples.target_text: Todo el dinero recaudado en el evento será utilizado en beneficio de los animales sin hogar.
